newsitem.title: FRANCE: France worried by Cambodian clashes, urges calm.
newsitem.headline: France worried by Cambodian clashes, urges calm.

text.p: France expressed concern on Saturday over clashes between rival government troops in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh and called for an immediate end to the fighting.

"France calls for the immediate cessation of violence and urges all sides to show restraint and a sense of responsibility in handling this dangerous situation," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
The French embassy in Phnom Penh has urged its nationals living in Cambodia to exercise caution, the statement added without providing details.

The fighting in Cambodia was particularly troubling as government officials had assured France of Phnom Penh's commitment to a peaceful pursuit of the political process during a meeting in Paris last Monday, the statement added.

Fighting broke out in Phnom Penh after Hun Sen, the country's powerful second prime minister, ordered a crackdown on "illegal troops" under the command of his rival, first Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Ranariddh was on the weekend in France, the former colonial power in Cambodia.
The two prime ministers head a deadlocked coalition government set up after United Nations-run elections in 1993.
A long-running row over power sharing between them has been inflamed in recent weeks by deep differences over how to deal with the divided Khmer Rouge guerrilla groups.
Neither of the prime ministers was in the country on Saturday. A Vietnamese official in Hanoi said Hun Sen was on vacation in Vietnam.
In Paris, Cambodian embassy officials confirmed that Ranariddh was in the French capital but could not confirm a French television report that he was trying to cut short his stay to return home.
